topic: Widespread loss of SNAP (food stamp) benefits nationwide
summary: SNAP participation has dropped by more than 4.5 million people (about 11%) between July 2025, when Trump signed the 'One Big Beautiful Bill Act' (OBBBA) reconciliation law, and April 2026. The law raised the work-requirement age ceiling from 54 to 64, added documentation burdens, cut off eligibility for several immigrant categories (refugees, asylum seekers, domestic-violence and trafficking survivors), and changed benefit-calculation rules -- on top of a separate, temporary withholding of benefits during the October-November 2025 government shutdown. This is a broad, ongoing nationwide trend rather than a single action -- see the related curated entries below for specific documented instances (a shutdown-specific funding freeze, a national child-impact analysis, and a state-level enrollment collapse in Arizona).

topic: Trump's personal net worth has grown substantially since returning to office, largely via crypto ventures
submitted_claim: trump made 2 billion dollars since becoming president
summary: Trump's personal wealth has grown substantially since his January 2025 inauguration, primarily through cryptocurrency ventures (World Liberty Financial, a Trump-branded stablecoin and meme coin) and licensing deals for branded products (Bibles, watches, sneakers, guitars, fragrances). The specific '$2 billion' figure in the submission isn't the number tracking sources actually support, though: estimates vary widely by which two dates are compared and are highly volatile because crypto holdings dominate the total -- Forbes-based reporting places the change anywhere from roughly flat ($6.7 billion at his January 23, 2025 inauguration vs. $6.6 billion in January 2026) to as much as a $4.1 billion increase measured from a 2024 pre-election baseline. This tracker separately documents two specific mechanisms behind that growth in more legal-rigor detail -- see related entries below.

topic: USS Abraham Lincoln's record-length deployment and reported crew welfare crisis
summary: The USS Abraham Lincoln, deployed to the Middle East since November 21, 2025 amid the Iran war, spent over 250 days at sea -- including more than 200 consecutive days without a port call, the longest continuous carrier deployment in the modern U.S. Navy. Multiple outlets reported a crew mental-health crisis severe enough that sailors attempted to go overboard, alongside food and water shortages and broken plumbing/sanitation. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth publicly called the reports 'completely misrepresented'; President Trump said the carrier had not been deployed 'nearly long enough.' Thirteen Senate Democrats, including the full Senate Armed Services Committee minority, sent Hegseth a formal letter demanding answers and a bipartisan congressional delegation visit. The Lincoln was relieved by the USS George Washington and began its return to San Diego around August 20, 2026.

topic: Claim that sailors are dying aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln
submitted_claim: sailors on the lincoln are dying
summary: Iran's Tasnim news agency reported on August 11-12, 2026 that seven U.S. sailors were killed and several wounded in a violent brawl aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln, a claim quickly amplified by other Iranian and Syrian state outlets (PressTV, SANA). U.S. Central Command flatly denied the report, stating 'this report is false' and that no service members aboard the carrier had died. CENTCOM did confirm a real, separate incident -- one sailor went overboard on August 3 and was quickly and safely recovered. The underlying story of a genuine crew-welfare crisis aboard the Lincoln (record-length deployment, mental-health strain, suicide-attempt reports, poor living conditions) is independently documented -- see the Community Topics entry on the deployment/crew-welfare crisis -- but the specific 'sailors are dying' claim traces to unverified wartime propaganda from Iranian state media, not any confirmed incident.

sources.name: Newsweek -- CENTCOM slams 'false' Iran claim that 7 sailors died in USS Lincoln brawl
